test_title: RRB NTPC CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 30 Jan 2021 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: What is the percentage of the paid up share capital held by the central government or by any state government or partly by the central governments and partly by one or more state governments in Public Sector Undertakings?
solution:
The correct answer is__** 51% or more.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Section 2(45)** of the **Indian companies act, 2013**, defines a government company as, **"Any company in which not less than ******51%** of the paid-up share capital is held by the central government, or by any state government."**
 
• The Central Government and partly one or more State Governments, from time to time these Companies are known as **Mixed Ownership Companies**.
 
• At least **51%** of the shares must be owned by the government in order to be a government company.
 
• Shares in a Government company can be clasped in the name of **the President of India or the Governor of a State**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ​**The subsidiary company** is the one in which another company grip more than 51% of the nominal value of its equity share capital or more than** 51 % of its voting power. **
 
• Government stock means **any stock issued by the Government or any funds of or annuity granted by the Government.**
 
• The Paid-up share capital of a company is **the amount of money for which shares were issued to the shareholder for which payment was made by the shareholder**.
